title: RES↔QA-001: Testability Feedback on Research Artifacts + Field-Failure Data for Research
description: The Researcher provides testable acceptance criteria with each Technology Transfer Pack (quantified, measurable criteria QA can independently verify — e.g., sensor SNR ≥ 45 dB under specified field conditions), test vectors and golden-reference outputs for transferred algorithms, documented known limitations and edge cases, and scientific context for complex validation scenarios; the QA & Test Automation Engineer provides testability feedback on research artifacts, validation-criteria gap analysis, independent verification of research claims (measured validation results), and field-failure data showing any gap between research-stage predictions and production reality. Grounded in IOT_EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_RESEARCHER_SKILL §6.10. The QA testability gap analysis is a soft pre-transfer gate; the binding production go/no-go remains QA's gate (see QA↔PO-001).

research_test_artifacts.description: RES→QA: testable acceptance criteria, test vectors, golden references, limitations.

unit.description: Explicit unit — criteria must be independently measurable (e.g., dB).

conditions.description: Specified field/environmental conditions for the measurement.

qa_research_feedback.description: QA→RES: testability assessment, gap analysis, independent verification, field-failure data.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine testability review and field-failure feedback is agent-autonomous (gap analysis within 10 business days; transfer validation within 15 business days). The QA gap analysis can require the Researcher to supplement before transfer is finalized; the binding production go/no-go remains QA's permanent gate (QA↔PO-001).
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + CALENDAR (testability review with gap analysis within 10 business days of TTP receipt; technology-transfer validation within 15 business days; research-relevant field-defect summaries in the quarterly Field Quality Report; ad hoc test-design consultation within 5 business days)
confirm_conditions: every acceptance criterion is quantified — metric, comparator, value, and explicit unit (independently measurable)
test vectors and a golden reference are provided for any transferred algorithm
known limitations and edge cases are documented in the Technology Transfer Pack
an INSUFFICIENT testability assessment returns a concrete validation-criteria gap list
reject_conditions: an acceptance criterion stated without a quantified value + unit (untestable — e.g., 'high SNR' instead of 'SNR ≥ 45 dB')
field-failure data that softens or omits a research-prediction-vs-production-reality gap (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
a productized research finding declared validated without measured independent-verification results
counter_conditions: a transferred algorithm lacks test vectors for parity validation — request the golden reference before validation
a complex validation scenario needs domain knowledge — request the scientific-context consultation before designing the test
